basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 30.' and it opens 'Vers. 30. Zara interpretatur Oriens, vel quia prior egredi debuit, vel quia ex illius'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 30. Zara interpretatur Oriens, vel quia prior egredi debuit, vel quia ex illius familia multi justi et sapientes exorti sunt. Allegorice per hos duos filios Judae duo populi figurantur; per Zaram, qui primus manum eduxit, Judaicus populus designatur, qui quasi manum praebuit, quando se praeparatum ad Dei mandata implenda ostendit. Cui obstetrix coccinum ligare voluit, id est fide Dominicae passionis et crucis illum insignire. Coccinum vero, quod sanguinis habet colorem, Christi indicat passionem. Sed ille manum | cruentatam sanguine prophetarum et ipsius Domini retraxit, quia fidem passionis ejus recipere noluit. Illo tardante, junior egressus est frater, hoc est, populus gentilis credendo in Christum ad obediendum praeceptis ejus se praeparavit.
